Currently
column2: host_rsp is cached on a per-vCPU basis

column1: struct vcpu_vmx.  In non-nested usage the caching is for all intents
and purposes 100% effective
column2: e.g. only the first VMLAUNCH needs to

column1: synchronize VMCS.HOST_RSP since the call stack to vmx_vcpu_run() is
identical each and every time.  But when running a nested guest
must invalidate the cache when switching the current VMCS as it can't
guarantee the new VMCS has the same HOST_RSP as the previous VMCS.  In
other words
column2: the cache loses almost all of its efficacy when running a

column1: nested VM.
Move host_rsp to struct vmcs_host_state
is cached on a per-VMCS basis and restores its 100% hit rate when
nested VMs are in play.
Note that the host_rsp cache for vmcs02 essentially ""breaks"" when
nested early checks are enabled as nested_vmx_check_vmentry_hw() will
see a different RSP at the time of its VM-Enter.  While it's possible
to avoid even that VMCS.HOST_RSP synchronization
dedicated VM-Exit stack
column2: there is little motivation for doing so as

column1: the overhead of two VMWRITEs (~55 cycles) is dwarfed by the overhead
of the extra VMX transition (600+ cycles) and is a proverbial drop in
the ocean relative to the total cost of a nested transtion (10s of
thousands of cycles).
